abstract: Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey, biweekly cycle 202620, published October 8, 2026. Question 7 asks whether a business used artificial intelligence in any of its business functions in the last two weeks; Question 24 asks whether it expects to within six months. This is the highest-frequency firm-side AI adoption measure in the US and the series jobsdata.ai plots on ai-adoption-rate. Values are dated to reference-period end, which for BTOS falls six to seven weeks before publication.
keyFindings: National AI use was 23.8 percent of firms (SE 0.41 percent) for the two weeks ending 2026-09-20, unchanged from 23.8 percent for the cycle ending 2026-09-06 - the first flat reading after four consecutive increases.
The six-month expectation of AI use (Q24) was 27.7 percent (SE 0.36 percent), up 0.1 points from 27.6 percent, so the gap between current and expected use held near 3.9 points.

The standard error widened from 0.26 to 0.41 percent between the two cycles, so this cycle's estimate is less precise than the one before it and a 0.0-point change is well inside sampling noise either way.
One flat cycle does not break the trend: AI use has risen from 21.5 percent for the cycle ending 2026-07-12 to 23.8 percent, and the level remains the highest in the series.
methodology: Biweekly establishment survey across a large national sample of about 1.2 million US businesses, published as an experimental data product. Each estimate is collected over a two-week window covering a two-week reference period ending six to seven weeks before publication; cycle 202620 was collected 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-04 for the reference period 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-20. The November 2025 rewording from AI use 'in producing goods or services' to 'in any business function' is a same-construct instrument change, and Census publishes one continuous series.
qualifiers: A firm-level adoption share, not a measure of how much work AI performs. It counts any use in the prior two weeks, so it sets a low bar per firm and says nothing about intensity - other surveys find that adopters apply AI to a minority of tasks. Not directly comparable to posting-based measures or to payment-based measures such as the Ramp AI Index, which read far higher on narrower or self-selected footprints. The biannual AI Supplement is a separate instrument with an 11-week reference window and should not be treated as the latest point in this series. The AI questions appear in every cycle; the press releases are boilerplate and never mention AI, so the National.xlsx workbook is the only reliable read.
